fields.body_md:
## About this programme

Thinking of a master's in computer science at Birmingham? Here is what it costs, who can get in and the 2027 deadlines.

The Computer Science MSc is a one-year, full-time conversion course. A conversion course teaches computing to graduates from other subjects. It started in 1969 and is taught in person at the Edgbaston campus, in English.

**The most important fact for you:** you need a degree in a subject other than computing. If you hold a BTech, BE or BCA in computer science, this course is not for you.

You take **180 credits**. Six core modules of 20 credits each cover Software Workshop 1 and 2, Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning, Building Useable Software, Computer Systems, and Data Structures, Algorithms, and Databases. In the summer you do a **60-credit** project. Every project builds and tests a large software system.

For the wider university, see our [University of Birmingham page](/study-abroad/universities/university-of-birmingham).

## Can you get in?

**Degree.** You need a 2:1 honours degree in any subject other than computing. A 2:1 is a UK honours grade. The university recommends A-level or at least GCSE grade A in Mathematics.

**Indian marks.** Birmingham's India page says a three- or four-year Indian bachelor's degree is considered. A 2:1 normally means **55% to 60%** or higher, depending on your university.

**GRE.** The course page does not mention GRE. GRE is a US-style graduate admissions test.

**English.** IELTS is an English language test. This course asks for **IELTS 6.5** with no less than **6.0** in any band. Other accepted results include:

- TOEFL iBT taken from January 2026: **4.5** overall, with **4.5** in any two skills and **4** in the other two
- TOEFL iBT taken before January 2026: **88** overall, with at least 21 Reading, 20 Listening, 22 Speaking and 21 Writing
- PTE Academic: **67**, with no less than **64** in all four skills
- Cambridge C1 Advanced: **176**, with no less than **169** in any part

If your offer asks for English, a pre-sessional English course at Birmingham can replace a retake.

**ATAS.** ATAS (Academic Technology Approval Scheme) is a UK security clearance that some science and technology courses need before you get a visa. Birmingham's course page does not say whether this course needs it. Ask the admissions team when you get your offer. If it is needed, an ATAS application takes at least **30 working days**.

## What it costs

Tuition for international students is **£36,000** for September 2027. A January 2027 start costs **£34,740**, but its visa deadline has passed.

Birmingham is outside London, so the outside-London visa rule applies. This is the worked first-year total.

| Item | Amount |
|---|---|
| Tuition for international students, September 2027 | £36,000 |
| Living money you must show for your visa: £1,171 × 9 months | £10,539 |
| Student visa application fee, from outside the UK | £558 |
| Immigration Health Surcharge for a visa of just over a year | £1,164 |
| **Total** | **£48,261** |

The sum is £36,000 + £10,539 + £558 + £1,164 = £48,261. Travel and housing are not included.

**Living money is money you show, not a fee.** The visa rule is **£1,171** for each month of your course outside London, up to **9 months**. You must hold this money for **28 days** in a row. The 28-day period must end within **31 days** of the date you apply. You do not pay it to the university.

**Health surcharge.** The Immigration Health Surcharge (IHS) is a charge for using the NHS while you are in the UK. It is set by the length of your visa, not your course. For a course of 12 months or longer, the visa adds up to **1 month** before and **4 months** after the course. That makes a visa of more than a year but under 18 months. You then pay the yearly **£776** plus half of it, **£388**, so **£1,164**.

**Deposit.** You pay a tuition fee deposit before the university issues your CAS. A CAS (Confirmation of Acceptance for Studies) is the electronic letter your visa application needs. The deposit comes off your tuition when you register. The amount shows in your applicant portal after an offer.

**Paying tuition.** You can pay in full or by instalments.

For the visa steps, read the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide). To plan the whole budget, use the [UK total cost breakdown](/study-abroad/study-in/uk/uk-total-cost-breakdown).

## Funding

No scholarship on this course page is open to Indian students for 2027 entry yet.

- **Postgraduate Chancellor's Scholarship for India:** **£10,000** off first-year tuition, but listed for September 2026 and closed.
- **Postgraduate High Fliers Scholarship:** **£5,000**, listed for September 2026 and closed.
- **Alumni Scholarship:** **£3,000** off tuition, only for returning Birmingham undergraduates. Deadline **31 July 2027**.

New awards for 2027 may appear later. Watch the [international scholarships page](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/international/fees/scholarships) and the course page.

## Deadlines and intakes

| Intake | Who applies | Deadline | Where to apply |
|---|---|---|---|
| September 2027 | International applicants who need a visa | 2 July 2027 | University online application |
| September 2027 | UK and non-visa applicants | 27 August 2027 | University online application |
| January 2027 | International applicants who need a visa | 30 October 2026 (passed) | University online application |

The page lists 2 July 2027 as the visa deadline next to the January box. The September non-visa date is 27 August, so 2 July 2027 is the one to use for September. Birmingham closes applications once the course is full, so apply early.

## How to apply

1. **Check the entry rule.** Make sure your first degree is not in computing and you have a 2:1 or equivalent.
2. **Apply online.** Submit your application and supporting documents online. Start from the [course page](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/subjects/computer-science-and-data-science-courses/computer-science-msc).
3. **Prepare your documents.** Have your degree certificate and transcripts, your English test result and any translations ready.
4. **Accept your offer and pay the deposit.** Meet your offer conditions. The university then issues your CAS.
5. **Check ATAS.** Ask the admissions team if the course needs an ATAS certificate.
6. **Apply for your visa.** You need your CAS, a current passport, proof of funds and your tuberculosis (TB) test result. India is on the UK's TB test list. The test must be at a clinic approved by the Home Office. Read the [TB test page](https://www.gov.uk/tb-test-visa/countries-where-you-need-a-tb-test-to-enter-the-uk) and the [UK student visa guide](/study-abroad/visas/uk-student-visa-guide).

## After the programme

- **Work in the UK after your course.** The Graduate Route lets you stay and work in the UK after your studies. The visa lasts **2 years** if you apply on or before **31 December 2026**, and **18 months** if you apply on or after **1 January 2027**. A September 2027 student applies in 2028, so expect 18 months. The application fee is **£937**.
- **Industry links.** The school works with The Alan Turing Institute, the UK's national institute for data science and AI.

## Who it suits

**This programme is a strong choice if:**

- your degree is in engineering (other than computing), science, commerce, law or arts, and you want a tech career
- you have a 2:1 or about 55% to 60% from your Indian university
- you want a one-year course with a large software project

**Think carefully if:**

- your degree is in computer science or IT, because the course is for non-computing graduates
- you are counting on a scholarship, because the India awards on the page are for 2026 and closed
- you need a January 2027 start, because that visa deadline has passed

Already studied computing? Birmingham's [Advanced Computer Science MSc](https://www.birmingham.ac.uk/study/postgraduate/subjects/computer-science-and-data-science-courses/advanced-computer-science-msc) asks for a 2:1 in Computing or a closely related subject. Its September 2027 fee is also **£36,000**.

- [Immigration Rules, Appendix Student](https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-rules-appendix-student). Checked on 4 November 2026.

faq_json.q: Can I do the Birmingham MSc Computer Science with a BTech in computer science?
faq_json.a: No. The course is a conversion course for graduates with a 2:1 in any subject other than computing. Computing graduates can look at Birmingham's Advanced Computer Science MSc.

faq_json.q: How much does the Birmingham MSc Computer Science cost for Indian students?
faq_json.a: Tuition is £36,000 for September 2027. Adding visa living money, the visa fee and the health surcharge gives £48,261 for the first year.

faq_json.q: What percentage do Indian students need?
faq_json.a: Birmingham's India page says a 2:1 normally means 55% to 60% or higher, depending on your university.

faq_json.q: What is the deadline for September 2027?
faq_json.a: 2 July 2027 if you need a visa, and 27 August 2027 if you do not. Applications close earlier if the course fills.

faq_json.q: Does Birmingham need GRE or IELTS for this course?
faq_json.a: The course page does not mention GRE. It asks for IELTS 6.5 with no less than 6.0 in any band, or an accepted equivalent such as PTE Academic 67.
